::: {.key-question}
What chronic health conditions are experienced by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander peoples in the NEPHU catchment?
:::

## Diabetes

### Self-Reported Diabetes

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diabetes, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
diabetes_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Health_Diabetes_LGA.csv",
                                  variable = "diabetes") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(diabetes != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
diabetes_lga <- diabetes_lga %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(diabetes = dplyr::case_when(
    diabetes == "Has diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes)" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = diabetes,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diabetes, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
diabetes_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Health_Diabetes_AgeSex.csv",
                                        variable = "diabetes") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(diabetes != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
diabetes_agesex <- diabetes_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(diabetes = dplyr::case_when(
    diabetes == "Has diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes)" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = diabetes,
                          dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 5.0% (n = 566) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have diabetes. This was similar to non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment (4.8%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have diabetes ranged from 97 (Hume LGA) to 5 (Manningham LGA).

- The percentage of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have diabetes ranged from 6.9% (Darebin LGA) to 1.8% (Manningham LGA).

- The number of people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have diabetes was highest for people aged 50-59 or 60-69 years for both males and females, and the percentage of people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have diabetes increased with increasing age.

- The gap between the observed number of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people who have been told by a doctor or nurse that they have diabetes and the expected number if the proportion was the same as for non-Indigenous people was particularly large for all age groups less than 70 years.

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultation during the development of this report, the association between healthy eating and the risk of diabetes was discussed.

- It was also noted that gestational diabetes is a separate condition that is not included in these data.

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- Data for this topic were collected from all people completing the ABS Census 2021.

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- `r note_aboriginality_census`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- People were classified as having diabetes if they selected *Diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes)*.

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Census respondents may have reported Type 1 and/or Type 2 diabetes.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Census questions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- Has the person been told by a doctor or nurse that they have any of these long-term health conditions? (*Select all that apply*)
  - Arthritis
  - Asthma
  - Cancer (including remission)
  - Dementia (including Alzheimer's)  
  - Diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes)
  - Heart disease (including heart attack or angina)
  - Kidney disease
  - Lung condition (including COPD or emphysema)
  - Mental health condition (including depression or anxiety)
  - Stroke
  - Any other long-term health condition(s)
  - No long-term health condition

:::

### Hospital Admissions for Diabetes

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - diabetes
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_diabetes <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_principal_diag",
                                                column_select = "admissions_for_diabetes_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_diabetes <- hospital_diabetes %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Social Health Atlas of Australia](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases), compiled from the [Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED)](https://www.health.vic.gov.au/data-reporting/victorian-admitted-episodes-dataset).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 504 hospital admissions for diabetes for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for diabetes for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 118 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 5 (Knox and Melbourne East IAREs).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for diabetes for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 1,234 per 100,000 population (Maroondah IARE) to 66 per 100,000 population (Melbourne East IARE).

- 4 of the 10 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area had an age-standardised admission rate for diabetes above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Maroondah, Whitehorse, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, and Moreland/Broadmeadows IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Admissions for diabetes were defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - E10: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
  - E11: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
  - E12: Malnutrition-related diabetes mellitus
  - E13: Other specified diabetes mellitus
  - E14: Unspecified diabetes mellitus

:::
